pr_title: roachtest: export sysbench results to roachperf
pr_body:
This change parses the results of sysbench tests to JSON, so they can be exported to roachperf.

Epic: https://cockroachlabs.atlassian.net/browse/CRDB-38187
Fixes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/123071
Release note: none

_________________________________________

See https://github.com/cockroachdb/roachperf/pull/167 for the corresponding roachperf PR.

issue_context.title: roachtest: add sysbench suite to roachperf
issue_context.body:
We run the following sysbench tests nightly:
```bash
➜ roachtest list sysbench
Listing tests which match regex "sysbench" and are compatible with cloud "gce".

sysbench/oltp_delete/nodes=3/cpu=32/conc=256 [test-eng]
sysbench/oltp_insert/nodes=3/cpu=32/conc=256 [test-eng]
sysbench/oltp_point_select/nodes=3/cpu=32/conc=256 [test-eng]
sysbench/oltp_read_only/nodes=3/cpu=32/conc=256 [test-eng]
sysbench/oltp_read_write/nodes=3/cpu=32/conc=256 [test-eng]
sysbench/oltp_update_index/nodes=3/cpu=32/conc=256 [test-eng]
sysbench/oltp_update_non_index/nodes=3/cpu=32/conc=256 [test-eng]
sysbench/oltp_write_only/nodes=3/cpu=32/conc=256 [test-eng]
```

These should be marked as benchmarks and uploaded to roachperf so that we can track performance over time and catch performance regressions.

Jira issue: CRDB-38187

review_comments: Should this be an error, or are there lines we don't expect to match? If latter, maybe we should count the number of parsed lines and log it, for ease of debugging; i.e., thinking about the case when all of a sudden we get an empty output, say due to a format change upstream.

Yeah there are lines we don't expect to match, there's additional output that isn't metrics, i.e.:

> Running the test with following options:
Number of threads: 256
Report intermediate results every 1 second(s)
Initializing random number generator from current time

I like the counting the number of lines idea, added a log + a safeguard case where we error if we get 0 output at all.
Not sure if this will actually solve the issue since I'm unable to repro it, but figured it's worth a try while I'm in the file already 😄
Yep, thanks for adding it. I am still rather curious what causes it. Evidently, it's been observed in the wild, but I am not sure the root cause is known.
